title: EventPipe framing adaptor and staggered reconnect strategy for function-call-safe streams
creator: Samantha Ortiz
description:
Goal: Implement an EventPipe framing adaptor and staggered reconnect strategy that preserves function-call and structured-output atomicity across interrupted SSE connections, while remaining compatible with legacy SSE clients.

Background: Customers often stream long outputs and use tool/function calling. Existing SSE reconnection approaches either drop partial semantic frames (breaking function-call atomicity) or require heavy client-side heuristics. This ticket defines a server-side framing + reconnect protocol that: (1) emits small, self-describing micro-chunks with provenance, (2) marks function-call boundaries and structured JSON records with explicit continuity markers, and (3) supplies compact resume tokens to enable safe reassembly on reconnect without losing atomic tool call events.

Design summary:
- Framing: output is emitted as JSONL micro-chunks with the following visible fields per chunk: chunk_id, prev_chunk_id (nullable), offset, sem_type (text|json|function_call|meta), payload (base64 or plain depending on flags), and optional checksum. Chunks include an event-level sentinel when starting/ending function calls or structured outputs.
- Continuity markers: add a lightweight continuity envelope 'continuity_hint' which indicates whether the chunk completes a semantic unit or is a mid-unit fragment. Clients can use this to buffer until a unit-complete marker arrives.
- Resume tokens: server issues short-lived resume tokens (opaque, HMAC-signed) that encode last-acknowledged-chunk_id, allowed TTL, and the model instance shard. Tokens are single-use by default and can be reissued for authorized rejoin.
- Staggered reconnect strategy: on client reconnect, a negotiation happens: client sends its resume token (if any) + last-seen-chunk_id. Server validates and returns an explicit reattach plan: either a delta stream from next_chunk_id, a resync snapshot (small state diff for long gaps), or a fallback full reemit for older clients. The reconnect sequence supports progressive backoff windows to avoid hot replays.
- Legacy compatibility: emit a parallel SSE-friendly event called 'eventpipe-compat' for legacy clients that expect raw text frames. Eventpipe-compat aggregates unit-complete micro-chunks into a single SSE text event. This is an optional server-side transform behind a feature flag.

Trade-offs considered:
- Overhead: micro-chunk metadata increases token/byte counts; mitigated by compacting fields and binary payload encoding when beneficial.
- Complexity: added protocol complexity both server and client-side. Mitigation: provide a lightweight reference JS client and Node SDK helper to decode/reauthorize resume tokens.
- Security: resume tokens expose continuity surface; mitigations include HMAC signing, short TTL, and per-customer scoping. Security review required.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server emits framed JSONL micro-chunks with continuity markers for function_call sequences in canary model.
- Reconnect negotiation returns correct delta stream for resume tests (unit tests + integration with websocket/SSE harness).
- Reference JS client can reattach and reconstruct function calls atomically in 95% of simulated packet-loss scenarios.
- Feature flag exists to enable eventpipe-compat transform for legacy clients.

Rollout plan: internal canary using dedicated capacity for two customers + automated chaos tests (socket drop, reorder, duplication). Gradual rollout behind feature flag and opt-in on console per project.

Docs & artifacts: design doc, protocol spec, example client code, security checklist, load test results. See links below.
